correctness.rationale: The defining signed radial symbol is an absolutely convergent L1 series, with norm at most 1/(30M). Gamma integration gives eigenvalues Phi_N(m/K)=(4(m/K)/(1+m/K)^2)^N, each nonnegative and at most min(1,4m/K,4K/m). Scale ratios >=16 yield uniformly bounded diagonal sum <=128/15 and spikes >=1 at distinct degrees K_j-1, so a positive bounded but noncompact operator. The Berezin coefficients are nonnegative. A unimodal Riemann-sum inequality and explicit beta integral bound yield sup_s B_{N,K}(s)<=16/sqrt(N)+12/K; choosing N_j=(j+1)^4 makes these suprema summable. Individual diagonal blocks are compact; their Berezin transforms vanish, and dominated convergence proves the full Berezin transform vanishes. L1 convergence and bounded fixed kernels justify termwise Berezin integration. The accompanying 333 exact rational checks verify finite identities; all infinite assertions have analytic proof. No operator-norm series convergence is assumed.

originality.rationale: Looi (arXiv:2608.09131), introduction and Sections 4–5, proves the broader nonradial L1 counterexample and real-symbol positivity, but explicitly excludes radial L1 symbols from the constructions (introduction, radial paragraph). The new inverse-Laplace example is radial in the symbol, not merely diagonal in an adapted operator basis; it realizes arbitrary small L1 mass with nonzero essential norm. Zorboska 2002 Theorem 0.4 is conditional, Korenblum–Zhu 1995 assumes bounded symbols, Zhou–Chen–Dong 2013 Theorem 10 imposes controlled diagonal oscillation, and the 2026 Li–Wang result assumes bounded symbols. Looi 2603.10879 treats an essential positivity/liminf question and does not provide this vanishing/noncompact radial case. No identical or dominating theorem was identified in these checked materials or the mathematical-record searches; older obscure moment constructions remain a priority risk.
residual_risks: An older unpublished or differently indexed radial moment construction may provide an equivalent counterexample; primary-literature and mathematical-record searches are not exhaustive.

value.rationale: The motivating 2026 paper explicitly identifies radial L1 symbols as an untreated natural subclass, despite settling the corresponding nonradial integrable-symbol question. A radial symbol forces diagonal Toeplitz structure, making the obstruction to Berezin detection more surprising, and the positive operator provides strong spectral control. The explicit family closes this natural boundary of the existing result, while its arbitrarily small L1 symbol norm and unit-height spectral spikes quantify instability. The proof supplies a reusable inverse-Laplace scheme and a true infinite-dimensional counterexample, not a routine finite example or numerical perturbation.
